line_status.note: Under the first aleph the print shows two side-by-side dots (tsere), not three (segol); under the second word's he the mark is a horizontal patach stroke, not two dots — so Reading A matches the print (and the MT/Thesaurus forms אֵהָב, אֹהַב).

The first root's initial letter is printed as he (ה, open at the top-left), not chet — consistent with the preceding line's "letters softened" (הב, אב) and Gesenius's comparison of הבל 'to breathe'. Reading B is correct; Reading A's חָבַל is wrong.
